AI BIJAN Motion - packed source files of this folder. Do not edit by hand.
The skill upload in the Claude app accepts at most 200 files, so the source files are packed here.
`node <skill folder>/new-project.mjs <project folder> --kit=<style>` unpacks them into the project.
Format: per file one line with four '=' signs, the byte length and the path, then exactly that many bytes.

==== 3083 src/kits/pixelstory/camera/CinematicCamera.tsx
import React, { createContext, useContext } from "react";
import { AbsoluteFill } from "remotion";

// A pinhole camera over flat layers placed at real distances. Dolly (z) scales near
// layers faster than far ones, pans shift near layers more than far ones, and depth
// of field is a circle of confusion computed from each layer's distance to the
// focus plane. Nothing here is a preset: the look comes from where things are.

export const FOCAL = 1000; // the subject plane: a layer at Z=1000 moves 1:1 with the camera
export const SCREEN = { w: 1080, h: 1920, cx: 540, cy: 960 };

export type CameraState = {
  /** Pan, in screen px at the subject plane. */
  x: number;
  y: number;
  /** Dolly toward the scene, in the same units as layer Z. */
  z: number;
  /** Roll, degrees. Used sparingly. */
  roll: number;
  /** Distance in focus. */
  focus: number;
  /** Blur in px for a layer twice the focus distance away. */
  aperture: number;
};

export const restCamera: CameraState = { x: 0, y: 0, z: 0, roll: 0, focus: FOCAL, aperture: 0 };

const Ctx = createContext<CameraState>(restCamera);
export const useCamera = () => useContext(Ctx);

/** Screen-space position of a point that sits on a layer at distance Z. */
export const project = (cam: CameraState, Z: number, px: number, py: number) => {
  const s = Z / Math.max(1, Z - cam.z);
  const k = FOCAL / Math.max(1, Z - cam.z);
  return {
    x: SCREEN.cx + s * (px - SCREEN.cx) - cam.x * k,
    y: SCREEN.cy + s * (py - SCREEN.cy) - cam.y * k,
    s,
  };
};

export const CinematicCamera: React.FC<{ cam: CameraState; children: React.ReactNode }> = ({ cam, children }) => (
  <Ctx.Provider value={cam}>
    <AbsoluteFill style={{ transform: cam.roll ? `rotate(${cam.roll}deg)` : undefined, transformOrigin: "50% 50%" }}>
      {children}
    </AbsoluteFill>
  </Ctx.Provider>
);

type LayerProps = {
  /** Distance from the camera at rest. */
  z: number;
  children: React.ReactNode;
  /** Extra blur on top of depth of field (atmospheric haze). */
  haze?: number;
  /** Cap on depth-of-field blur, px. */
  maxBlur?: number;
  style?: React.CSSProperties;
};

export const Layer: React.FC<LayerProps> = ({ z, children, haze = 0, maxBlur = 28, style }) => {
  const cam = useCamera();
  // A layer at or behind the lens is not in the picture. Rendering it would mean a
  // scale in the hundreds (and, with blur, a texture the browser can't rasterise).
  if (z - cam.z < 24) return null;
  const dz = z - cam.z;
  const s = z / dz;
  // Magnified past ~14× a layer is a blur filling the lens; skip it rather than rasterise it.
  if (s > 14) return null;
  const k = FOCAL / dz;
  const coc = Math.min(maxBlur, cam.aperture * Math.abs(z - cam.focus) / Math.max(1, cam.focus) + haze);
  return (
    <AbsoluteFill
      style={{
        transform: `translate(${-cam.x * k}px, ${-cam.y * k}px) scale(${s})`,
        transformOrigin: `${SCREEN.cx}px ${SCREEN.cy}px`,
        filter: coc > 0.35 ? `blur(${coc.toFixed(2)}px)` : undefined,
        ...style,
      }}
    >
      {children}
    </AbsoluteFill>
  );
};

==== 1676 src/kits/pixelstory/camera/path.ts
import { fbm1 } from "../core/noise";
import { keys, springFollow, type Ease } from "../core/motion";
import { restCamera, type CameraState } from "./CinematicCamera";

type Channel = keyof CameraState;
export type CamKey = { f: number; e?: Ease } & Partial<CameraState>;

/**
 * Keyframed camera. Each channel interpolates only between the keys that set it,
 * so a dolly and a tilt can start and end at different times.
 */
export const cameraAt = (frame: number, ks: CamKey[], base: CameraState = restCamera): CameraState => {
  const out = { ...base };
  for (const ch of Object.keys(base) as Channel[]) {
    const track = ks.filter((k) => k[ch] !== undefined).map((k) => ({ f: k.f, v: k[ch] as number, e: k.e }));
    if (track.length) out[ch] = keys(frame, track);
  }
  return out;
};

/**
 * Operator drift: the slow, low-amplitude float of a camera on a fluid head.
 * Not shake — periods are seconds long and amplitudes are a few pixels.
 */
export const drift = (frame: number, seed = 1, amp = { x: 4, y: 3, roll: 0.06 }) => ({
  x: fbm1(frame / 140, seed) * amp.x,
  y: fbm1(frame / 170, seed + 9) * amp.y,
  roll: fbm1(frame / 200, seed + 21) * amp.roll,
});

/** Lagged tracking of a moving subject — the camera follows motivation, late and smooth. */
export const follow = (
  frame: number,
  target: (f: number) => { x: number; y: number },
  opts: { start?: number; stiffness?: number; damping?: number } = {},
) => {
  const o = { start: opts.start ?? 0, stiffness: opts.stiffness ?? 40, damping: opts.damping ?? 13 };
  return {
    x: springFollow((f) => target(f).x, frame, o).value,
    y: springFollow((f) => target(f).y, frame, o).value,
  };
};

==== 1175 src/kits/pixelstory/character/spark.ts
// A spark: one pixel of a drawing that wakes up. Its heart is teal — the palette's
// only colour for "alive" — wrapped in gold light.

import { sprite, type Palette, type Sprite } from "../pixel/sprite.ts";

export const SPARK_PAL: Palette = {
  c: "#C9FFF4", // core
  t: "#3FB7A8", // living heart
  y: "#FFE9BC", // hot glow
  g: "#F4B860", // gold
  a: "#E8892E", // amber rays
};

const SIZES: Sprite[] = [
  sprite(["c"]),
  sprite([".g.", "gcg", ".g."]),
  sprite(["..a..", ".gyg.", "aytya", ".gyg.", "..a.."]),
  sprite(["...a...", "...g...", "..gyg..", "agytyga", "..gyg..", "...g...", "...a..."]),
  sprite([
    "....a....",
    "....g....",
    ".a..y..a.",
    "...gyg...",
    "agyytyyga",
    "...gyg...",
    ".a..y..a.",
    "....g....",
    "....a....",
  ]),
];

/** Pick a size (0–4); `twinkle` toggles the diagonal glints on twos. */
export const sparkSprite = (size: number, twinkle = false): Sprite => {
  const s = SIZES[Math.max(0, Math.min(SIZES.length - 1, Math.round(size)))];
  if (!twinkle || s.w < 9) return s;
  return { ...s, cells: s.cells.map((c, i) => ((i === 19 || i === 25 || i === 55 || i === 61) && c === "a" ? "." : c)) };
};

==== 3379 src/kits/pixelstory/core/motion.ts
// Deterministic motion primitives. Every function is a pure function of the frame,
// so any frame can be rendered in isolation and in any order.

export type Ease = (t: number) => number;

export const clamp = (v: number, a = 0, b = 1) => Math.min(b, Math.max(a, v));
export const lerp = (a: number, b: number, t: number) => a + (b - a) * t;
export const invLerp = (a: number, b: number, v: number) => clamp((v - a) / (b - a));
export const remap = (v: number, a: number, b: number, c: number, d: number, ease: Ease = linear) =>
  lerp(c, d, ease(invLerp(a, b, v)));

export const linear: Ease = (t) => t;

// Curves are named by intent so scenes read like direction notes.
export const ease = {
  linear,
  // Camera: long, heavy, no visible start or stop.
  camera: (t: number) => (t < 0.5 ? 16 * t ** 5 : 1 - (-2 * t + 2) ** 5 / 2),
  cameraSoft: (t: number) => (t < 0.5 ? 4 * t ** 3 : 1 - (-2 * t + 2) ** 3 / 2),
  // Arrivals: fast in, long settle.
  arrive: (t: number) => (t === 1 ? 1 : 1 - 2 ** (-10 * t)),
  arriveSoft: (t: number) => 1 - (1 - t) ** 3,
  // Departures: slow start, accelerating exit.
  depart: (t: number) => (t === 0 ? 0 : 2 ** (10 * t - 10)),
  departSoft: (t: number) => t ** 3,
  // Mechanical lock with a small overshoot.
  lock: (t: number) => {
    const c1 = 1.4;
    const c3 = c1 + 1;
    return 1 + c3 * (t - 1) ** 3 + c1 * (t - 1) ** 2;
  },
  // Organic in-out for body motion.
  body: (t: number) => -(Math.cos(Math.PI * t) - 1) / 2,
  // Snappy anticipation: dips below 0 before going.
  anticipate: (t: number) => {
    const c = 1.7;
    return t * t * ((c + 1) * t - c);
  },
  smooth: (t: number) => t * t * (3 - 2 * t),
} satisfies Record<string, Ease>;

/** 0→1 progress between two frames with an easing curve. */
export const ramp = (frame: number, from: number, to: number, e: Ease = linear) =>
  e(invLerp(from, to, frame));

export type Key = { f: number; v: number; e?: Ease };

/** Piecewise keyframes; each key's easing shapes the segment that ends on it. */
export const keys = (frame: number, ks: Key[]): number => {
  if (frame <= ks[0].f) return ks[0].v;
  for (let i = 1; i < ks.length; i++) {
    const a = ks[i - 1];
    const b = ks[i];
    if (frame <= b.f) {
      const t = (frame - a.f) / (b.f - a.f);
      return lerp(a.v, b.v, (b.e ?? ease.body)(t));
    }
  }
  return ks[ks.length - 1].v;
};

/**
 * Damped spring that chases a driver signal, simulated from `start` to `frame`.
 * Used for follow-through on secondary parts (cowlick, antennae, hanging cards):
 * they respond to the parent's motion instead of running their own loop.
 */
export const springFollow = (
  driver: (f: number) => number,
  frame: number,
  { start = 0, stiffness = 180, damping = 12, mass = 1, fps = 60, substeps = 2 } = {},
) => {
  let x = driver(start);
  let v = 0;
  const dt = 1 / fps / substeps;
  const end = Math.max(start, Math.floor(frame));
  for (let f = start; f < end; f++) {
    const target = driver(f + 1);
    for (let s = 0; s < substeps; s++) {
      const a = (-stiffness * (x - target) - damping * v) / mass;
      v += a * dt;
      x += v * dt;
    }
  }
  return { value: x, offset: x - driver(end), velocity: v };
};

/** Step a continuous value to a limited frame rate, the way sprite animation holds poses. */
export const onTwos = (frame: number, step = 2) => Math.floor(frame / step) * step;

==== 1536 src/kits/pixelstory/core/noise.ts
// Seeded randomness and smooth noise. No Math.random anywhere in the system.

export const hash = (n: number) => {
  let x = Math.imul(n ^ 0x9e3779b9, 0x85ebca6b);
  x ^= x >>> 13;
  x = Math.imul(x, 0xc2b2ae35);
  x ^= x >>> 16;
  return (x >>> 0) / 4294967296;
};

export const hash2 = (a: number, b: number) => hash(Math.imul(a | 0, 73856093) ^ Math.imul(b | 0, 19349663));

/** Seeded generator for building sets (book spines, tile orders, star fields). */
export const rng = (seed: number) => {
  let s = seed >>> 0 || 1;
  return () => {
    s ^= s << 13;
    s ^= s >>> 17;
    s ^= s << 5;
    return (s >>> 0) / 4294967296;
  };
};

const fade = (t: number) => t * t * t * (t * (t * 6 - 15) + 10);

/** 1D value noise in [-1, 1]. */
export const noise1 = (x: number, seed = 0) => {
  const i = Math.floor(x);
  const f = x - i;
  const a = hash(i + seed * 1013) * 2 - 1;
  const b = hash(i + 1 + seed * 1013) * 2 - 1;
  return a + (b - a) * fade(f);
};

/** Fractal 1D noise, for drifts and flicker that never visibly loop. */
export const fbm1 = (x: number, seed = 0, octaves = 3) => {
  let sum = 0;
  let amp = 0.5;
  let freq = 1;
  for (let o = 0; o < octaves; o++) {
    sum += noise1(x * freq, seed + o * 17) * amp;
    amp *= 0.5;
    freq *= 2.03;
  }
  return sum;
};

// 4×4 Bayer matrix, normalised to (0,1). Used to dither between colour-ramp steps.
const BAYER4 = [0, 8, 2, 10, 12, 4, 14, 6, 3, 11, 1, 9, 15, 7, 13, 5];
export const bayer = (x: number, y: number) => (BAYER4[(y & 3) * 4 + (x & 3)] + 0.5) / 16;

==== 3360 src/kits/pixelstory/core/palette.ts
// Lamplight Diorama palette. Shadows are wine-black, never neutral; teal is reserved
// for things that are alive (a spark's heart, a creature's glow, living tiles).

export const C = {
  ink: "#0D0809",
  char: "#1B1115",
  wine: "#3D141D",
  burgundy: "#6B1F2D",
  crimson: "#9A2F35",
  ember: "#C2501F",
  amber: "#E8892E",
  gold: "#F4B860",
  glow: "#FFE0A6",
  ivory: "#F3E6CC",
  ivoryDim: "#CDBB9C",
  teal: "#3FB7A8",
  tealDeep: "#1F6B66",
} as const;

export type RGB = [number, number, number];

export const hexToRgb = (hex: string): RGB => {
  const h = hex.replace("#", "");
  return [
    parseInt(h.slice(0, 2), 16),
    parseInt(h.slice(2, 4), 16),
    parseInt(h.slice(4, 6), 16),
  ];
};

export const rgbToHex = ([r, g, b]: RGB): string =>
  "#" +
  [r, g, b]
    .map((v) => Math.max(0, Math.min(255, Math.round(v))).toString(16).padStart(2, "0"))
    .join("");

export const mixHex = (a: string, b: string, t: number): string => {
  const A = hexToRgb(a);
  const B = hexToRgb(b);
  return rgbToHex([A[0] + (B[0] - A[0]) * t, A[1] + (B[1] - A[1]) * t, A[2] + (B[2] - A[2]) * t]);
};

export const rgba = (hex: string, a: number): string => {
  const [r, g, b] = hexToRgb(hex);
  return `rgba(${r},${g},${b},${a})`;
};

// Material ramps for per-pixel relighting, darkest → brightest. Each ramp is hue-shifted:
// shadows drift toward wine, highlights toward gold, the way warm practical light behaves.
export const RAMPS = {

  plaster: ["#0f0a0c", "#1d1216", "#2d1a1d", "#432422", "#5f3426", "#84492c", "#ae6735", "#d99248"],
  paper: ["#16100f", "#2e2220", "#4b3833", "#6e564a", "#9a7c63", "#c4a47f", "#e6caa0", "#fbe9c8"],
  metal: ["#0b0809", "#17110f", "#251a16", "#38261c", "#503424", "#6e472d", "#946337", "#be8846"],
  book1: ["#0e0708", "#1d0b0f", "#2f0f16", "#45141d", "#5f1b25", "#7f2530", "#a3343c", "#c44c48"],
  book2: ["#0b0a09", "#1a1410", "#2c2016", "#3f2d1b", "#574021", "#755827", "#99752f", "#c49a3f"],
  book3: ["#08090a", "#101415", "#18201f", "#1f2c29", "#283a35", "#344b43", "#476152", "#647c63"],
  leaf: ["#07090a", "#0d1310", "#141d14", "#1d2a18", "#2a3a1b", "#3d4f1f", "#566826", "#76852f"],
